patch.name: Machine room hum (loop)
patch.description: The plant room in the basement of an office block: a transformer humming with its buzzing upper partials, a big extraction fan turning behind a grille, air pushing through the ducts, and now and then a contactor clacking somewhere in a cabinet. Concrete walls, so everything is a little boxy. The extraction surges and eases once a loop. The loop holds a whole number of hum cycles and fan turns, and the seam is crossfaded.

tracks.note: The transformer: mains hum with strong upper partials (so it is audible on small speakers), driven for buzz, and a slow beat between its cores.

The extraction fan: an electric motor, a soft drone with a blade-passing whine (`teeth` stands in for the blades). Its level heaves in and out once per loop (the surge gain), as if the extraction were fighting a door opening somewhere.
Air in the sheet-metal ducts: steady noise ringing faintly in a long tube. The "room tone" between the tones. It surges with the fan.
Contactors in the switch cabinets: a hard plastic-and-metal clack now and then. They break up the drone and say "this place is running".

controls.label: Hum
controls.hint: A faint electrical presence to a transformer you feel in your teeth.

controls.label: Ventilation
controls.hint: Still air to a roaring extraction system.

controls.label: Surge
controls.hint: Steady air to an extraction that heaves in and out once a loop.

controls.label: Activity
controls.hint: A plant ticking over at night to switchgear clacking constantly.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: A small cupboard of a room to a long concrete hall.

patch.name: Spaceship engine room (loop)
patch.description: The engine room of an old long-haul freighter under way: the reactor core throbs slowly, a deep unstable tone that never quite repeats, the plasma conduits sing a slow swirling chord above it, coolant hisses through the pipes, and a status panel pings to itself in the corner. Steel walls, a tank of a room. A stereo loop; the throb and the swirl are tied to the loop length and the seam is crossfaded.

tracks.note: The reactor: a Lorenz attractor as a low tone that wanders between two states, driven hard, then swelling in a slow throb (the throb comes after the drive, so the saturation cannot flatten it). Alive and slightly worrying.
The plasma conduits: a detuned FM chord with a slow phaser sweep, the "technology" above the rumble.
Coolant and air handling: a band of hiss that drifts, so the room has air in it.
A status panel: sparse, soft, high pings at slightly different pitches. Scale and a sign of life.

controls.label: Power
controls.hint: Drifting on standby to engines at full burn: higher, harder and brighter.

controls.label: Instability
controls.hint: A healthy, steady core to one that lurches and growls.

controls.label: Conduits
controls.hint: Bare rumble to a singing, swirling chord over it.

controls.label: Hull
controls.hint: A cramped crawlway to a cavernous steel hold.

controls.label: Systems
controls.hint: Dead consoles and still air to a busy, hissing, pinging room.

patch.name: Bird tweet
patch.description: A robin-sized songbird on a branch a little way off, one phrase: four clear whistled notes that each swoop down and flick up, drifting higher, then a short, soft dry trill that tumbles down and stops. The wood answers softly.

tracks.note: The whistled notes: a nearly pure tone from the syrinx with a fast swoop in each note. The second voice of the syrinx adds a faint shimmer above.
The rattle that ends the phrase, after the whistles: quick falling chips, the whole run sliding down. The Trill control sets how loud and long it is.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A tiny wren to a blackbird: lower, rounder notes.

controls.label: Tempo
controls.hint: A lazy song to a hurried one.

controls.label: Melody
controls.hint: Every note the same, to a phrase that climbs and wanders.

controls.label: Trill
controls.hint: Whistles only, to a long rattle at the end.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: On your windowsill to far off in the wood.

patch.name: Critter chirp
patch.description: A palm-sized furry critter asking a question: two quick squeaks from a tiny throat, "pri-rip?", the second one higher and curling up at the end, with a fast throat flutter, then a wet little sniff. Close, dry, in a burrow.

tracks.note: The voice: a tiny throat squeaking twice. The pitch curve is the question mark; the flutter makes it furry, not a whistle.
A short wet sniff after the question: breath only, through the same small throat. Mute it and the critter is less alive.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A mouse-sized squeaker to a fat guinea pig: lower and rounder.

controls.label: Question
controls.hint: How far the second squeak jumps up: flat and bored to a startled "eep?".

controls.label: Flutter
controls.hint: The purring roll in the throat: a clean peep to a rolled "prrr".

controls.label: Sniff
controls.hint: The wet sniff after the squeaks, from none to a snuffly nose.

patch.name: Ghostly moan
patch.description: Something that used to be a person, sighing in an empty stone church: a breathy "oooh" with no chest in it that darkens through "ü" to a covered "ö", a cry that drops, rises once more and sinks away, rough with a growl, and a second voice a little out of tune. A cold draught moans low through the stones beneath it. Most of what you hear is the building.

tracks.note: The voice: slack folds, half breath and a heavy growl that roughens it; the vowel darkens from "oo" through "ü" to a covered "ö". The vibrato that fades in is the sorrow.
Cold air through a gap: noise ringing in a narrow tube, low-passed with a little resonance, so it moans low under the voice instead of whistling.

controls.label: Sorrow
controls.hint: A flat, empty sigh to a wailing lament: deeper vibrato, a tighter throat and a shakier voice.

controls.label: Voice
controls.hint: A lost child, a woman, to a hollow old man.

controls.label: Menace
controls.hint: A sorrowful sigh to a rough, growling throat.

controls.label: Breath
controls.hint: A sung tone to almost nothing but air.

controls.label: Draught
controls.hint: Still air to a cold wind moaning under the voice: louder, and less muffled as it grows.

controls.label: Beyond
controls.hint: In the room with you, to far away on the other side.

patch.name: Insect fly-by
patch.description: A fat bumblebee crossing in front of your face from left to right, passing close to the nose: a fast wing buzz, never quite steady, bending down as it passes and fading into the garden. Stereo.

tracks.note: The wing beat: a narrow pulse wave that wanders in pitch and flutters in level as the insect corrects its flight, moved past the listener.
The papery rustle of the wings themselves: thin noise chopped at the wing rate, heard only when it is close.

controls.label: Insect
controls.hint: A whining mosquito, through a housefly, to a heavy bumblebee.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: Drifting past to zipping by: a bigger, quicker pitch drop.

controls.label: Closeness
controls.hint: Across the garden to brushing your ear.

controls.label: Nerves
controls.hint: A calm cruise to a frantic, zigzagging buzz.

patch.name: Kaiju roar
patch.description: A skyscraper-sized monster roaring over a city, made the way the classic one was: a resined glove dragged down a slack bass string, slowed down. A metallic shriek climbs, holds and wavers, then falls away slowly, on top of a chest roar far below it and a blast of air. The roar hits the far buildings and comes back a moment later.

tracks.note: The signature: a bowed, gritty string with a pitch arc, pushed through a giant mouth. This is what makes it a kaiju and not a lion.
The body under the shriek: a kaiju-sized throat growling far below it, driven so its harmonics give laptops the weight too.
The air leaving a mouth the size of a bus: a noise swell that peaks with the shriek and outlasts it a little.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A dinosaur to a monster that blocks out the sky: everything drops and slows.

controls.label: Shriek
controls.hint: How much of the metallic scream rides on top: a deep bellow to a piercing screech.

controls.label: Rage
controls.hint: A tired call to a furious, distorted, air-blasting roar.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Standing under it to hearing it from across the bay: more city echo, less top.

patch.name: Monster growl
patch.description: A bear-sized beast warning you off from the back of its den: a chest-deep growl that swells, opens from "oo" to "ah" as the lips pull back, rattles there, then sinks and closes. Hot breath hisses through the teeth the whole time. Heard close, in a rock chamber.

tracks.note: The growl itself: a big throat with period-doubled folds (growl) and a rattle in level that quickens at the peak. Pitch rises with the threat and sags at the end.
Air through wet teeth: pink noise shaped by the same mouth opening. It carries the growl on small speakers.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A big dog to something that fills the cave: deeper chest, longer throat.

controls.label: Anger
controls.hint: A low warning rumble to a torn, snarling threat with bared teeth.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A short grunt of a growl to a long drawn-out one.

controls.label: Den
controls.hint: Right at your ear to deep inside an echoing rock chamber.

patch.name: Robot creature chatter
patch.description: A knee-high maintenance droid with opinions: a short burst of burbling electronic speech, syllables of unstable tone that jump in pitch like words, squeezed through a small plastic speaker-mouth, ending on a rising two-note "bee-woop?". Its arms and head jerk about on little servos as it talks, and the head tilts as it finishes. Close, in a corridor.

tracks.note: The speech: two cross-modulating oscillators whose pitch is thrown to a new value on every syllable, each syllable a little chaotic. Seeds change what it says.
The sign-off: two clean notes, the second sliding up. It turns noise into a sentence with a meaning.

Its arms and head jerking about while it talks: small servo moves scattered through the speech, each at its own moment, speed and strength (the seed decides). Low-passed, so they are darker and softer than the head tilt at the end.
The head tilting as it finishes the question: a small geared motor. Gives the voice a body.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A pocket-sized bot to a barrel-shaped one: lower voice, bigger mouth.

controls.label: Talk speed
controls.hint: Slow, deliberate words to an excited gabble.

controls.label: Expression
controls.hint: A monotone drone to wild leaps of pitch.

controls.label: Glitch
controls.hint: A healthy clean voice to a damaged, crackling one.

controls.label: Servo
controls.hint: How loud its motors are: the twitches as it talks and the head tilt at the end.

controls.label: Fidget
controls.hint: Still while it talks to jerking about on every other word: from a single servo twitch to many.

patch.name: Slime squelch
patch.description: A fist-sized blob of slime dropping onto a stone floor and pulling itself together: a soft rubbery splat, then the wet suck of its skin peeling off the stone (a mouth-like "shhluck" that closes), while a handful of fat bubbles pop inside it. Close, with no room around it.

tracks.note: The body landing: a dead rubber skin hit softly. No ring, only a round, low thump that sags in pitch.
The squelch: a dense swarm of tiny wet pops (drops, not hiss) through a small mouth that goes from open to closed, so it says "shluck". The vowel sweep is the stickiness; the drops are the wetness.
Air pockets popping in the goo: rising-pitch drops, densest and loudest first. They make it thick liquid, not water.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A drip of goo to a bucket-sized blob: lower, fatter bubbles and a heavier splat.

controls.label: Stickiness
controls.hint: A quick wet slap to a long, reluctant peel.

controls.label: Bubbles
controls.hint: Smooth jelly to a fizzing, popping mass.

controls.label: Wetness
controls.hint: Thick and dull to thin, glistening and splashy.

patch.name: Door latch click (hollow-core)
patch.description: A cheap, light hollow-core bedroom door flicked shut on a carpeted landing: more pock than thud. First the bolt of the small tubular latch knocks back off the strike plate, a light, higher tack. Then it springs into the keeper, the lower and louder half of the ka-chunk, a dead rattly clack with pressed steel and plastic in it. At almost the same instant the thin door skins slap the stop and the cardboard-honeycomb cavity between them answers: a boxy, hollow pock, gone almost at once, with very little weight under it. Then the loose skin and the handle buzz against the frame for a moment. The room is small and soft: carpet, a short dull answer.

tracks.note: Both halves of the ka-chunk from one small mechanism: a tiny burst of noise through a short metallic resonator with a clustered chord, so each hit is a dense clack with no clean partial. First the bolt knocking back (higher, softer), then springing home (lower, louder).
The thin door skin slapping the stop: a damped sheet of hardboard with crowded modes, hit flat with something soft, then a small bounce. The pock of the door.
The hollow inside the door answering the slap: a short burst of low noise ringing a stubby tube, the boxy colour that says the door is empty.
The loose skin and the handle chattering against the frame after the hit: a thinning burst of small dull wooden and metal ticks.

controls.label: Hollowness
controls.hint: A thin flat slap, to an empty boxy pock like knocking on the door.

controls.label: Door size
controls.hint: A cupboard or wardrobe door, to a full-height room door.

controls.label: Push
controls.hint: Clicked gently to, or flicked shut so the door slaps and the two halves of the click run together.

controls.label: Latch
controls.hint: A tiny tinny catch, to a chunkier, duller mechanism.

controls.label: Rattle
controls.hint: A snug door, or one that chatters in its frame after it lands.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: Dry and close, a carpeted bedroom, or a bare landing.

patch.name: Heavy steel door slams
patch.description: A heavy steel security door (cell block, bunker, plant room) thrown shut in a bare concrete corridor, heard from a few metres inside. First the slab swings in, pushing a low gust of air ahead of it, its dry hinge giving one short quiet creak. Then the door meets its steel frame: a massive, dead BOOM from the slab and the wall it hangs in, a hollow boxy bark from the door skin, and a hard, dense, crashing clang from edge on frame that the door's own mass soon chokes. Loose hardware chatters in the frame, and the spring bolt drops into its keep with a two-part ka-chunk. The corridor throws it all back: a slap off the far wall and a long, hard, bright concrete tail.

tracks.note: Air pushed ahead of the swinging slab: a low gust that swells and is cut off by the slam. No tone in it.
One short dry creak from the hinge pin just before the hit: steel dragged on steel, irregular, quiet. Turn Hinge up for a rusty door.
The mass: slab and wall taking the blow. A soft-struck, heavily damped steel box, very low, whose pitch sags, driven so its weight also shows on small speakers.
The hollow door skin barking: a burst of noise ringing in the box of the door. This is what says 'big hollow steel thing' on a laptop.
Edge on frame: a dented steel plate with crowded modes, set off by a crumbling noisy contact so it crashes rather than rings, and choked by the door's mass.
Loose hardware shaken by the blow: hinge pins, the viewing flap, the bolt in its guides. A short, thinning burst of small steel ticks.
The spring bolt: 'ka' as it rides over the strike plate, 'chunk' a moment later as it drops into the keep. A short fat steel lump, lower and deader than the clang.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A sheet-steel locker-room door, up to a vault slab: the boom drops, lasts longer and takes over from the clang.

controls.label: Force
controls.hint: Pushed to until it meets the frame, or hurled shut: more crash, more bite on the edge, more air ahead of it.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: A gasketed door that lands with a dead thunk, or bare steel on steel that clangs on.

controls.label: Latch
controls.hint: No lock at all, or a big bolt slamming home later and louder after the hit.

controls.label: Rattle
controls.hint: A tight, well-hung door, or one with loose pins and plates that chatter after the blow.

controls.label: Hinge
controls.hint: Greased and silent, or a dry hinge that creaks as the door swings in.

controls.label: Space
controls.hint: An outside yard with nothing to answer, through a concrete corridor, to a deep stairwell that roars for seconds.

patch.name: Wooden door creak (low groan)
patch.description: A massive oak cellar door on wooden pintle hinges, leaned open very slowly: no squeal at all, only wood groaning against wood. Each slip of the hinge is a small knock that the door leaf answers with its own woody resonances. The slips come one by one at first ('tok, tok, tok'), crowd together into a rattling purr and fuse into a low, straining groan as the door passes the middle, with a catch where it drops and recovers. Then it slows back through the purr to single knocks and stops, the timber settling with a low thud. A second, smaller joint (the top pintle) ticks along at its own slower pace.

tracks.note: The lower hinge driving the door leaf: a modal wooden plate scraped over evenly spaced ridges, one ridge per slip, so `exciter.density` is the slip rate. Only a few modes that all ring equally long (low `damping`): few, narrow resonances are what turn a pulse train into a voiced groan instead of a zip.
The top hinge: a smaller, higher wooden joint slipping at a slower rate, never fast enough to fuse, so dry ticks ride on top of the groan and the two never line up.
The weight of the door: low thuds of the frame taking the strain at the start, lightly on the way, at the catch, and when it comes to rest.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: Leaned open slowly, knock by knock, or shoved open in one short groan.

controls.label: Groan
controls.hint: Separate slow knocks that never join up, or a higher, tighter groan close to a moan.

controls.label: Dryness
controls.hint: Waxed wood that purrs evenly, or parched, gritty wood that shudders and scrapes.

controls.label: Door size
controls.hint: A small hatch with a high wooden voice, or a huge gate with a deep one and heavy thuds.

controls.label: Hollow
controls.hint: A dead, dense slab that only knocks, or a thin resonant panel that hums and sings with every slip.

controls.label: Cellar
controls.hint: Close and dry, or echoing in a stone cellar.

patch.name: Big boom with debris
patch.description: A fuel depot goes up some way off. The explosion is built the way film sound does it: a sharp, complete bang recorded 'small' (a crack, a drum-like thump and a burst of fire noise) is played back slowed down, so everything in it becomes slow, low and enormous: the crack stretches, the boom takes its time to fall, and the fire roars on. Then the debris comes down: lumps of rubble thudding and clacking, big pieces first. Last, a big broken slab of stone lands with a dull crash and clatters to rest in closing bounces.

tracks.note: The crack and fireball, before slowing: bright noise with a fast-closing filter. Varispeed stretches it into a long, low roar.
The body: a drum skin struck hard, pitched like a tom, then slowed by the same factor so it lands deep, with its overtones intact.
What comes down: individual pieces of rubble, each a small dull lump of stone landing (no piece too short, and the tops rolled off, so they thud and clack instead of clicking), big ones first.

One large piece that lands late and clatters to rest: a broken slab of stone, a dented plate with crowded, heavily damped modes, set off by a rough noisy contact, so each landing is a dull crash with no note; the bounces close up and fade, each on a different edge (pitch jitter).

controls.label: Scale
controls.hint: A car backfire-sized bang to a slow, city-shaking detonation.

controls.label: Fire
controls.hint: A dry thud, or a long roaring fireball over it.

controls.label: Debris
controls.hint: Nothing thrown, to a long rain of wreckage.

controls.label: Open air
controls.hint: Close and dry to rolling across a wide open site.

patch.name: Distant explosion in a valley
patch.description: Artillery landing far away on the other side of a mountain valley, heard from a hillside on a still evening. There is no crack: the air has taken all the highs. What arrives is a soft, wide 'whump' of low noise, felt as much as heard, with a second, weaker arrival just behind it by another path (the 'ka-rump' of far guns). Then the valley plays with it: an echo off the near slope, another off the far wall, each darker and softer, over a low ground roll that heaves and wanders and takes a long time to die.

tracks.note: The blast as it arrives: a soft-edged burst of brown noise whose lowpass closes as it goes, then a weaker second arrival. Noise, so it is a pressure 'whump' and not a drum note; tube drive and a low-mid lift keep it alive on small speakers.
The weight under the whump: a very large slack skin set off by a short push of noise, sagging in pitch and soon gone. Kept well under the noise so no note hangs in the valley.
The rumble that follows along the ground: brown noise, slowly heaving (random tremolo, wander on the cutoff), kept low.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Near enough to keep a knock and some grit, to far beyond the ridge: only a slow soft pressure.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A mortar round's short bump to a magazine going up: lower, longer, with more ground roll.

controls.label: Echoes
controls.hint: Flat open plain, one thump, to a deep valley that answers again and again.

controls.label: Valley width
controls.hint: A narrow gorge with quick echoes to a wide basin with slow ones.

controls.label: Rumble
controls.hint: Just the thump and its echoes, or a long ground-rolling rumble after it.

patch.name: Firework rocket
patch.description: A rocket at a town display, watched from the square. The fuse lights and it leaves the tube with a short fizzing 'fsst'. It climbs, screaming: a whistle (noise in a narrow pipe) that rises with a fast warble and thins as it gets higher and farther. A moment of silence. Then the shell bursts high overhead: a broad, unpitched 'BOOM' of noise that opens bright and closes dark, a heavy hollow thump under it and, for a big shell, a deep rumble of pushed air rolling on after it. Then the stars, later the bigger the shell: a long spell of thick crackling spread across the sky as they burn out, drifting down, while the bang rolls back off the buildings round the square.

tracks.note: Lift-off: a fizz of violet noise and a small hollow thump from the mortar tube.
The screamer: noise forced through a tube resonator that climbs. The fast warble is the whistle composition burning unevenly; the gain curve is the rocket getting farther away.

The shell breaking, the main event: a burst of white noise whose lowpass falls fast from bright to dark, saturated. Broadband, so it is a bang and not a drum; the `height` lowpass is the air between the shell and the square.
The thump under the bang: a slack membrane pushed by a short burst of noise, damped so it sags and is soon gone. Weight only; it must not ring as a note.
The size of the shell: the deep push of air from a big break, a low rumble that rolls on under the bang and past it. A small shell hardly has it; Shell size brings it up.
The stars burning out (they catch later the bigger the shell), the signature of a firework: crackle that stays thick for a while after the burst and then thins, spread across the sky.

controls.label: Height
controls.hint: A low garden rocket, bursting soon and bright, to a big shell high up: a longer climb and a duller, later boom.

controls.label: Shell size
controls.hint: A small pop of colour to a huge aerial shell: a longer, deeper bang, a rumble you feel, and a bigger sky of crackling stars that take longer to catch.

controls.label: Whistle
controls.hint: A silent climb, or a loud screaming one.

controls.label: Crackle
controls.hint: A plain burst, or a long glittering crackle of stars.

controls.label: Town
controls.hint: Open field to a square ringed with buildings throwing the bang back.

patch.name: Grenade
patch.description: A fragmentation grenade bursting in soft earth a short way off, in open country with a treeline. First the detonation, a hard clipped crack with no pitch at all. Right on it the blast body, a burst of dark noise that closes fast (a 'KRAK-whump', not a note), and the ground taking the blow as a dead, crowded thud. A fountain of soil hisses up and out while steel splinters whip past and clack off stones; then clods and soil thud back down, thinning out. The treeline hands the bang back, dull, and it rolls on a moment.

tracks.note: Detonation: a very short burst of hard-clipped white noise. High explosive is a shock, not a boom: this sets the scale and is the loudest instant.
The pressure wave: pink noise through a fast-closing, wandering lowpass, saturated so it is a thick, ragged, broad 'whump'. Noise, so it has weight but no note.
The earth taking the blow: a huge damped slab (crowded modes, the lowest filtered away) struck with a contact spread out in time, so it is a dead pitchless thud under the blast.
The fountain of soil going up: a dense spray of tiny grit ticks, densest at once and soon gone. A dry 'pshh' that makes it earth and not a drum.
Steel splinters hitting stones and trunks: short dead clacks and ticks, no ring. Scattered through the moments after the blast.
A few splinters whipping past the listener: short falling zips, quiet. Follows the Shrapnel control.
Clods and soil raining back: dull little lumps (stone grains kept low and short, lowpassed), big ones first, thinning out.

controls.label: Charge
controls.hint: A flash-bang's short bark to a satchel charge: darker, longer, heavier, more ground in it.

controls.label: Punch
controls.hint: A soft whump to a chest-hitting slam with a hard crack on the front.

controls.label: Shrapnel
controls.hint: A plain blast, or steel splinters zipping past and clacking off everything.

controls.label: Dirt
controls.hint: Hard ground, nothing thrown, to a fountain of soil hissing up and thudding back down for a long time.

controls.label: Roll
controls.hint: Flat and dry, or echoing back off a far treeline and rolling.

patch.name: Firecracker pop
patch.description: A single firecracker going off on a pavement a few steps away. First the bang, a hard unpitched crack of full-band noise that darkens almost at once as the paper tube bursts, with a short low thump of pushed air under it. On the bang, the tube itself: a dead hollow cardboard colour, gone at once, never a note. Then shreds of paper and grit patter down on the pavement, while a hard echo comes back off the house across the street, duller, then a short street tail.

tracks.note: The bang: clipped white noise, full-band for an instant and then closing fast. Unpitched; this is the firecracker.
The push of air: a short burst of low-passed pink noise whose filter closes. Gives the bang weight without a pitch.
The paper tube bursting: a dented cardboard pipe with crowded, heavily damped modes, set off by a short burst of rough noise. A hollow colour on the bang that says 'small and paper', not a 'pok'.
Paper and grit landing: sparse dry ticks, thinning out.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A toy cap, a tiny snap, to a fat banger with a hollow thump.

controls.label: Snap
controls.hint: A dull damp pop to an ear-stinging crack.

controls.label: Shreds
controls.hint: Paper and grit raining down afterwards.

controls.label: Street
controls.hint: Open field, no echo, to a narrow alley slapping it back.

patch.name: Footsteps: leather shoes on concrete
patch.description: A loop of eight steps in leather shoes down a polished concrete corridor, at a slow walk, no two alike. Each step: the stacked leather heel lands with a short, hard, dry knock (a crowd of damped modes with a tiny tick on its leading edge, not a note) and the slab answers with a dead low thud; a beat later the sole rolls down with a softer, duller pat and a pinch of grit crushed under it; the corridor gives each a short dark slap. Left and right feet differ, some steps are mostly heel and some mostly sole, and each is a little bigger or smaller, a little early or late. Speed takes it from a slow walk to a run, where the heel barely touches and the forefoot slaps down hard right behind it. The loop is exactly eight step intervals long and wraps seamlessly.

tracks.note: Heel strike, every step: the stacked leather heel block, small, hard and well damped: many crowded modes that die almost at once, so it knocks and does not ring. Left and right heels are not equal (accents), and each step is a little bigger or smaller (pitch).
The hard edge of the heel meeting concrete: a tiny burst of bright noise, the 'tick' of a dress shoe. Its own accents: some steps land on the edge and tick, some land flat and barely do.
The floor answering each step: a concrete slab is a huge plate, so a dead crowd of low modes gives the step its weight without a note. Follows the heel's accents; running hits it harder.

The sole rolling down off the heel, a beat later when walking: a soft, duller leather pat. Its accents run against the heel's, so some steps are mostly heel and some mostly sole. Running, it lands right behind a light heel touch and becomes the hard forefoot slap.
Dust and grit crushed under the sole as it rolls: a small burst of fresh grains on every step, never the same twice, and on some steps almost none (accents).

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow walk to a run: the steps come faster, the heel-to-toe roll closes up into a hard forefoot slap and the floor is hit harder.

controls.label: Shoe
controls.hint: A soft sneaker that pads, to a dress shoe, to a hard stiletto click.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A light quick step to a heavy stomp.

controls.label: Grit
controls.hint: A swept, polished floor with clean placed steps, to a dusty one where every sole crunches and drags.

controls.label: Corridor
controls.hint: Dry and close, or a long empty corridor slapping back.

patch.name: Footsteps: sneaking on a creaky wooden floor
patch.description: A loop of eight steps: someone creeping across the old boards of a quiet house at night, trying not to be heard. Each step is eased on, slowly and never evenly, since they wait and listen: the edge of the foot finds the board with a small pat, the sole rolls down with a soft brush, and a moment later the floor takes the weight with a dull, hollow press and no heel knock at all. The boards give them away, each in its own voice: one rubbing on its nail draws a climbing whine, a thin one gives a short, dry, high squeak, a loose end clacks on its joist, and once a thick board lets out a long low groan, the loudest thing in the loop, the one to freeze on. Some steps are silent but for the press, and later ones meet the whining and the squeaking board again, at other pitches. A creak is stick-slip, not a voice: each slip is a small knock that the board answers with its own few narrow wooden resonances, heard one by one where the board starts and stops moving (a quick tick-tick) and fused into a tone in between. Speed takes the same floor from this sneak through a walk to a run: thumping forefoot steps, evenly spaced, the loose board rattling and the creaks cut short and pitched up, the boards slipping faster.

tracks.note: The foot finding the board: the edge of a socked or soft-soled foot set down first, a small dull pat. Running, it is the slap of the forefoot.
The weight eased on: the sole rolling down from the edge to flat, a soft brushing swell with no impact in it. It is most of what a careful step sounds like, and nearly gone at a run.

The floor taking the weight: boards over a hollow, a big wooden panel, so a crowd of low modes and no single pitch. Sneaking, the blow is spread out and soft, a dull press; running, it is a hard thump.
A loose board, on a couple of the steps: its free end knocks the joist as the weight comes on. Small, damped and dented, so a dry clack and not a note. Running rattles it harder.

The complaining board, on a couple of the steps: it rubs on its nail as the weight comes on. Stick-slip: each slip is a small knock that the board answers with its own few narrow wooden resonances (a `modal` plate scraped over ridges, `exciter.density` the slips per second). It starts as a quick tick-tick, fuses into a climbing tone, catches, starts again and slows as the weight settles. The step's pitch jitter retunes the board, so each creak is a different board.

A thin dry board, on a couple of the steps: a short high squeak that rises as the slips speed up and stops dead when the board catches. A small, thin wooden bar with only a few modes, so it squeaks rather than knocks.

The board that gives you away, once in the loop: a thick plank with a deeper, crowded ring, loaded slowly, so the slips stay slow enough to hear one by one at the ends (a ratcheting 'crrr') and fuse into a low, straining groan in the middle, with a catch partway through. Long, and the loudest thing in the loop: the one to freeze on.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow walk to a run: creeping with long uneven waits, a careful sneak, then thumping, evenly spaced running steps with short sharp creaks.

controls.label: Creak
controls.hint: A sound floor that only thumps, a few boards that complain, or a floor where nearly every step groans long and loud.

controls.label: Board
controls.hint: Thick old beams that groan low, to thin dry boards that squeak.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A cat-light tread to a heavy man: a louder, lower, longer press from the floor.

controls.label: Shoe
controls.hint: Bare feet and socks, or hard soles that tap and knock.

controls.label: House
controls.hint: Close and dry, or an empty room answering each step.

patch.name: Footsteps: gravel
patch.description: A loop of eight steps in boots on a loose, damp gravel path, outdoors, no echo, here at a run. Each step: the heel digs in and a run of small stones grinds and clicks, thick at first and quickly thinning, on a dull, dead thump of the packed ground; the ball of the foot rolls forward with a longer, finer crunch and a little grit is thrown off the toe; under both, the gritty grind of the sole sinking in. Every crunch is a different handful of stones, left and right feet weigh differently, each step is a little bigger or smaller, earlier or later, and twice in the loop a stone is kicked away and hops to rest. At a run, as here, the steps close up, heel and toe land almost together, the crunch is shorter and harder, the ground thumps and gravel sprays behind each landing; Speed takes it back to a slow, careful walk where the toe rolls in well after the heel. The loop is exactly eight step intervals long and wraps, so it repeats without a seam.

tracks.note: Heel crunch: a thick run of small stones knocking together, coarse and loud, thinning as the heel beds in. New stones every step.
Toe roll: a longer, finer, quieter crunch as the foot rolls forward and pushes off, overlapping the heel so the step is one event. Running, it lands with the heel and is cut short.
The boot sinking in: the continuous gritty rub of stones sliding under the sole, flickering at random, which fills the gaps between the separate clicks.
The packed earth under the stones: a dull, dead thump (a crowd of low modes, no note) so the step has a body. Harder and louder at a run.
Grit thrown off the toe: a thin burst of fine stones landing just after push-off, barely there at a walk and uneven from step to step; at a run it is the spray of gravel behind each landing.
The odd stone kicked away: twice in the loop a pebble is knocked forward by the toe and hops to rest.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow walk to a run: the steps close up, heel and toe land together, and gravel sprays.

controls.label: Stones
controls.hint: Fine grit and sand to coarse river pebbles that clack.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A child tiptoeing to a soldier with a pack.

controls.label: Loose stones
controls.hint: A raked, settled path to a deep loose drive where stones are kicked away and scatter.

controls.label: Wet
controls.hint: Dry dusty gravel, crisp and bright, or rain-soaked and dull.

patch.name: Footsteps: metal grate
patch.description: Eight steps of work boots running along a steel catwalk deep inside a steel hull, as a seamless loop. Each step: the rubber heel lands with a dull thud and the heavy grating panel clanks, a dense, sour, low clang of many crowded bars, no one note; a moment later the panel knocks down onto its frame and its bars tick against each other; the ball of the foot follows with a lighter second clank, at this pace so close behind the heel that the two close to one hard clang. No two steps are alike: the feet differ in weight and timing, and most steps land on a sound panel but some on a shorter, bent one that chatters on its clips. At a run the rattle grows and the catwalk under the panels hums; Speed takes it back to a slow walk, where heel and toe come apart. The hull answers each step, hard and metallic.

tracks.note: The boot itself, every step: a soft rubber heel thud under the clank. It carries the weight of the walker.
The sound panel, under most of the steps: a heavy welded lattice struck by a rubber heel. A big panel, so the modes are low, crowded and dented: a sour clank, not a ting.
The next panel along, under the other steps: a shorter, more bent panel that sits badly in its frame, so it clanks higher, duller and shorter. It is the one that rattles.
The ball of the foot rolling on after the heel: a lighter, softer second clank struck nearer the middle of the panel. Running closes the gap to a flam and makes it the main blow.
The panel knocking down onto its frame a moment after the heel: one small, dead steel knock on every step.
The bars of the lattice ticking against each other after each blow: a short sprinkle of small dead steel ticks, new ones every step.
The loose panel chattering on its clips, only on the steps that land on it: one piece of steel bouncing to rest, its knocks closing up.
The catwalk itself, the stringers and handrail the panels sit on, shaken by every step: a low, dull, dented hum that is barely there at a walk and builds when running.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow walk to a run: quicker steps, heel and toe closing to one hard clang, more rattle and the catwalk starting to ring.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A light quick tread to a heavy armoured stomp.

controls.label: Loose
controls.hint: A tight, well-clipped deck that only clanks, or panels that knock and clatter in their frames.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: Thick damped plate that clunks, to thin grating that sings on after each step.

controls.label: Panel
controls.hint: Small stair treads to long spans of walkway.

controls.label: Space
controls.hint: An open-air gantry, or deep inside a steel hull.

patch.name: Footsteps: puddles (loop)
patch.description: Rubber boots walking slowly through shallow puddles on a street: a loop of eight steps, no two alike. Each step: the boot comes down through the water onto the asphalt with a dull thud that the water mostly hides, and the flat of the sole hits the surface a moment later. The water answers with a wet splash: a dense crackle of tiny pops of drops and bursting skins, each a very short ring, through a resonance that moves as the water sloshes, densest at first and quickly thinning, with a soft edge of mist over it, only a sprinkle of bigger bubbles, and a small "shlop" under it as the water is shoved aside and falls back. Then the thrown water plips back into the puddle drop by drop, thinning to the odd last drop, and as the boot lifts a few small drops fall off it. The puddles differ: some are barely wet, the deepest gulps with fat bubbles, and only some steps drip. Speed goes from a slow, careful wade to a run through standing water.

tracks.note: The boot meeting the asphalt under the water: a dead, crowded thud with no note, far under the water. In the reference recordings it is barely there; Stomp brings it up, and deeper water buries it further.
The flat of the sole slapping the surface, just after the heel when walking: a very short wet smack that closes down at once. Only the contact: the water that follows is in the other layers.

The water thrown up as the sole hits it: a dense crowd of tiny wet pops (water drops and bursting skins, each a very short ring whose pitch rises), not hiss. They pass through a resonance that moves as the water sloshes, so the splash has a shape, "splsh", instead of a flat spectrum: densest at the start and quickly thinning.
A few air bubbles caught under the sole popping up through the splash: small rings whose pitch rises, well above the deep gulps. Only a sprinkle: dense, they turn the step into a cartoon 'bloop'.
Only in the deeper puddles: a few fat bubbles gulping up round the boot, low and slow. Silent on the shallow steps, full on the deepest.

Water shoved aside by the boot and falling back into the hole: dark noise in a hollow that opens (pitch falls) then fills (pitch rises), a short "shlop" with no clear note. Bigger in the deeper puddles.
The fine mist thrown off the edge of the splash: a short, soft hiss well under the drops, only there to give the splash its edge.
The thrown water falling back onto the puddle: separate drops plipping into the water, short wet rings rather than ticks, thick at first and thinning to the odd last drop.
Water running off the boot as it lifts, and the puddle settling: a few separate small drops in the gap before the next step, high and quiet. Some steps shed none.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow walk to a run: the steps come faster, the foot lands flat and hard, and each one throws more spray and leaves less time for drips.

controls.label: Depth
controls.hint: A wet pavement to ankle-deep puddles: more shlop and fat low bubbles, a lower and longer splash, less street under it.

controls.label: Splash
controls.hint: A careful step that barely breaks the surface, or a stamp that throws water everywhere: a bigger, longer crackle, more spray and more drops landing.

controls.label: Stomp
controls.hint: A soft wade in, or a hard flat slap of the sole on the water.

controls.label: Drips
controls.hint: Dry boots, or boots that shed drops back into the puddle after every step.

controls.label: Street
controls.hint: Open and dry-sounding, or between wet walls.

patch.name: Footsteps: snow
patch.description: A loop of eight steps in boots through deep fresh snow on a still winter day, at a slow, careful walk. No impact anywhere: each step is a soft press, the weight sinking into the pack in a few pushes as the heel, the ball and the toe go down, and no two alike: one stops short, the next settles on and on, thick or sparse. A muffled low whumpf carries most of it, with a fine, quiet, grainy crunch of compacting snow over it that swells with each push; after it a few loose crystals trickle back into the print. Every step is a different handful of grains, left and right feet weigh differently, each is a little bigger or smaller, earlier or later; on a few steps the boot breaks through a thin frozen crust with faint brittle snaps, twice it brushes through the surface on its way forward, and a little powder comes off the toe. Snow swallows sound, so it is close and dead with no echo. Speed takes it from a slow trudge to a run: quicker, shorter, harder presses and snow kicked up behind nearly every stride. The loop is exactly eight step intervals long and wraps, so it repeats without a seam.

tracks.note: The snow compacting under the sole: a mass of tiny ice bonds giving way, a fine, quiet, grainy crunch. Its density wanders freely within each step and differs from step to step. Fine grains, not pops: separate loud clicks turn snow into gravel.

The heel and the ball of the foot going into the snow pack: a soft, muffled low press with no attack. Its pushes and its colour are drawn fresh every step (a random flutter on the level, a wandering filter), so no two presses are alike.

The foot settling deeper as the weight rolls onto the toe: a random handful of low, soft pushes (puffs of low band noise), sometimes none and sometimes several, landing anywhere in the moments after. How many there are and where they fall is drawn fresh each step, so some steps stop short and others sink on and on, thick or sparse. Louder steps sink further.
Loose crystals trickling back into the footprint once the foot is down.
Only on some steps: the boot breaks through a frozen crust, a few sharp brittle snaps as the plate gives, just as the foot lands.
Snow kicked up off the toe as the foot leaves: a soft bright puff that falls away. Faint and uneven at a walk; thrown on nearly every stride at a run.
Only on a couple of walking steps: the boot drags through the top of the snow on its way forward, a soft swish before it lands. Gone at a run.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: From a slow trudge to a run: steps close up and land harder and shorter, and snow is kicked up behind each stride.

controls.label: Cold
controls.hint: Wet, heavy snow that sounds dull and close, to dry powder with a bright, crisp crunch.

controls.label: Depth
controls.hint: A dusting over hard ground, or knee-deep drifts: each step a longer, lower press.

controls.label: Crust
controls.hint: Soft fresh snow with nothing to break, or an icy crust that snaps under the boot on some steps.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A child's light step to a heavy walker in big boots who sinks at every step.

patch.name: Body punch
patch.description: A film-style punch to the ribs, miked close. First the sleeve cuts the air, a short swish rising in pitch; then the fist sinks in, a wet leathery smack on top of a dead, crowded thump of flesh and a chesty 'oof' of displaced body (no note, sagging as the chest gives), with a dull cracked knuckle-on-rib knock inside it; all of it is over almost at once, squeezed hard like a movie fight.

tracks.note: The arm coming: a brief rush of sleeve and air before the hit, rising, cut off by it.
The thump: a soft dead mass the fist sinks into rather than strikes. Many crowded, dented modes that die at once, so it is a thud, not a drum; the pitch sags as the body gives.
The weight a laptop can play: the chest cavity giving, a burst of dark noise whose filter closes fast.
Skin and cloth: the wet slap on top, the part laptop speakers carry.
Knuckles on ribs: a short, cracked woody knock inside the thump.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A jab to a heavyweight body blow: lower, fatter, a little longer.

controls.label: Smack
controls.hint: A muffled hit through a coat, or a bare wet slap.

controls.label: Bone
controls.hint: All soft tissue, or a crack of knuckle on rib.

controls.label: Swing
controls.hint: A short jab with barely a rustle of sleeve before it, or a long telegraphed swing you hear coming.

patch.name: Cardboard box dropped
patch.description: A half-full cardboard box dropped from knee height onto a laminate floor. It lands on one bottom edge with a dead papery whump; a moment later it tips flat with a second, softer and lower thump and the slap of its face on the floor; from just after the first landing, the things inside (books, clothes) slide and knock against the walls. No ring anywhere: cardboard eats it.

tracks.note: The box: a dead cardboard cavity. Two events: the edge lands, then it tips flat.
The flat face slapping the floor: papery mid noise, on the second landing.
What is inside, sliding and knocking the walls.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A shoebox to a wardrobe carton.

controls.label: Contents
controls.hint: Empty, or packed with things that slide and knock.

controls.label: Hard stuff
controls.hint: Soft clothes and books inside, or cutlery and tins.

controls.label: Drop
controls.hint: Set down gently to dropped from the shoulder: harder, with a livelier tumble.

patch.name: Coin dropped and settling
patch.description: A large coin dropped a hand-width onto a wooden table top. It lands on its edge with a bright ring and hops, faster and faster and a little wild because it is spinning; then it falls onto its face and wobbles briefly round its rim, a faint rattle speeding up and rising in pitch as it flattens, and stops dead. The table knocks softly under the first hits.

tracks.note: The coin bouncing on its edge: one small metal disc, each hop sooner and softer.
The spin-down: the coin rolling round its rim, faster and higher until it lies flat.
The table top under the first hits: a soft wooden knock that gives it a place.

controls.label: Coin
controls.hint: A tiny thin coin that tinks to a heavy silver dollar.

controls.label: Height
controls.hint: Slipped from the fingers, or dropped from standing: longer hops.

controls.label: Spin
controls.hint: Lands flat and stops, or spins down in a long rising rattle.

controls.label: Table
controls.hint: Stone counter with no voice, or a hollow wooden table that knocks.

patch.name: Knock on a wooden door
patch.description: Knuckles on a panelled interior door, heard from the hallway side: three raps in a hand's rhythm, the first the firmest and each one a touch later and softer. Each rap is a bony knuckle click, then the whole door leaf answering with a dense, dry, pitchless knock (a crowd of damped modes) and the hollow of the panel giving a short boxy cough; the room behind the door returns a short muffled bloom.

tracks.note: The door leaf: a big wooden plate whose lowest modes are too low to hear, so the knock is the crowd above them, damped and dented, with no note. High-passed because a door barely radiates the deep bass. The envelope only fades the inaudible low modes out before the voice ends.
The hollow of the panel: a short puff of noise coughing in a shallow box. This is what says 'door' and not 'table'.
Bone on wood: the small hard, slightly cracked click on top of each rap.

controls.label: Knocks
controls.hint: One rap to five.

controls.label: Urgency
controls.hint: A slow polite tap to fast hard pounding.

controls.label: Door
controls.hint: A thin hollow-core door that barks and booms, to a thick oak one that gives a short dead knock.

controls.label: Room behind
controls.hint: Nothing behind the door, or an empty room that answers.

patch.name: Giant metal slam
patch.description: A blast door the size of a house dropping shut in an empty hangar, heard from fairly close. First the slab falls the last metre in its guides, steel shrieking low on steel, air rushing out from under it. Then thousands of tons of plate meet the sill, not a clang but a crumbling, crowded CRASH, with the concrete floor taking the blow as a dead pitchless boom. The slab bounces and settles, two smaller, lower landings, while the plate groans as it grinds to rest in its frame and shaken-loose bolts and scale rain onto the floor. The hangar answers a beat behind with a dark roar whose low end clears first.

tracks.note: The last metre of the drop: the slab dragging down its guides, a low ragged steel shriek that speeds up and rises, with no clear note. Cut off by the landing.
Air squeezed out from under the falling slab: a dark gust that swells into the hit.

The door meeting the sill: a huge dented steel plate with a great crowd of modes, landing along its whole edge so the blow is spread out, and set off by crumbling noise, so it crashes instead of tolling. Two smaller landings follow as it bounces and settles.
The weight: the concrete floor slab taking the blow, a soft wide landing on a crowd of dead low modes with no note, driven so small speakers show it.
The crumbling part of the crash: scale, sill and sheet steel breaking up, a noise burst that darkens as it dies.
The slab grinding to rest in its frame: a big steel plate dragged over grit, the catches slowing as it comes to rest, its pitch sagging.
Bolts, scale and rust shaken loose, raining onto the floor after the landing, thick at first and thinning.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A shipping container door to a dam gate: lower, longer, more floor in it.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Standing under it, or hearing it from the far end of the hall: more roar, less edge.

controls.label: Debris
controls.hint: A clean close, or bolts and rust raining after it.

controls.label: Rust
controls.hint: New machined steel that lands with a long clang, or a corroded wreck that shrieks down, crunches and grinds.

controls.label: Hall
controls.hint: A big workshop to an endless cavern.

patch.name: Two glasses clink
patch.description: Two wine glasses touched rim to rim in a toast, close to the ear at a dinner table. The two bowls are slightly different sizes, so two clear notes a little apart ring together; the second glass speaks a hair after the first; each is not quite round, so its note shimmers; the wine inside dulls the top of the ring.

tracks.note: Your glass: the lower note.
Their glass: a little smaller and thinner, a hair late.
The contact itself: a dry glassy tick.

controls.label: Glass size
controls.hint: Shot glasses that tink to big balloon glasses that sing low.

controls.label: Fill
controls.hint: Empty crystal that rings on, or full glasses whose ring is short and dull.

controls.label: Toast
controls.hint: A careful touch to an enthusiastic clack.

controls.label: Mismatch
controls.hint: A matched pair on one note, or two odd glasses far apart.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: Dry at the ear, or across a dining room.

patch.name: Glass shatters
patch.description: A small window pane smashed in with a bar, heard from inside a tiled kitchen. The bar meets the pane and the glass lets go all at once, a hard, bright crash: the sheet rings out as it cracks and bursts into a mass of pieces. Then the pieces keep coming, pouring out of the frame and raining onto the tiles: a sparse glitter of separate pieces, each heard on its own as it clinks and rings on, thin and high, with no hiss under it, and larger shards bouncing among them. It holds up for a while, then thins quickly to the last few splinters ringing faintly on their own.

tracks.note: The pane giving way: the sheet of glass itself, rung hard along a crack, a bright glassy crash with a clear, short ring in it.
The pane bursting into a mass of pieces at once: a dense burst of small glass plates, each with its own short, high ring, so the first moment is a wall of glittering clinks rather than a hiss.
The bar meeting the pane in its wooden frame: a low knock under the break, small next to the glass.

The pieces pouring out of the frame and raining down: thick at first, thinning to a scatter, each a clink that rings on, lower than the glitter, so every piece is heard on its own. Big pieces lower and louder, small ones higher and fainter, and a few loud ones over a quiet bed.

The fine splinters among the pieces: a sparse sprinkle of pure, high rings that each ring on a while, over the whole rain and thinning with it. This is what makes the cascade sound like glass and not gravel.

Clumps that hung on in the frame breaking loose and landing: a fresh burst of ringing pieces each time, the waves in the cascade, fainter as it ends. A small pane has few to lose, so they are barely there; Size brings them up.
Larger shards landing on the tiles among the rain: a few pieces spread over the cascade, each bouncing to rest in a quickening chatter of dry clinks.
The last splinters settling after the rain has stopped: a few tiny pieces ringing clear and high on their own, faint, at the very end.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A drinking glass to a shop window: lower, longer, the pieces falling for longer.

controls.label: Pieces
controls.hint: A clean break into a few big pieces, or an explosion of splinters.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: Carpet that swallows the pieces, or hard tiles they dance on.

controls.label: Force
controls.hint: A crack that lets go slowly, or a violent smash.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: Dry, or a hard tiled room.

patch.name: Metal pipe struck
patch.description: A length of steel scaffolding pipe gripped in one fist, struck near its end with a wrench in a concrete garage. First the steel-on-steel tick; then the pipe rings on its bar modes, slightly out of round so its partials beat, but the grip chokes the ring short; under it the air inside the pipe answers with a short hollow bonk; the garage returns a hard slap.

tracks.note: The pipe itself: a steel bar hit near the end, slightly bent so the partials beat. The hand gripping it damps the ring; Grip lets it hang free and sing.
The air column inside: a wrench tick ringing a hollow tube, the "bonk" that says pipe and not rod.
The first instant of steel on steel: a tiny bright tick.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A short offcut that pings to a long heavy pole that tolls.

controls.label: Strike
controls.hint: A rubber boot heel to a steel wrench: duller and rounder, or brighter with a hard tick.

controls.label: Grip
controls.hint: Hanging free and singing, or clamped in a fist so the ring chokes at once.

controls.label: Hollow
controls.hint: A solid bar, or a wide pipe whose air column bonks.

controls.label: Garage
controls.hint: Dry and close, or ringing off the concrete walls.

patch.name: Rock on rock
patch.description: A fist-sized river stone thrown down onto a boulder in a dry gorge. First a hard, bright, pitchless CRACK, the small stone's click and a splintering snap of grit on top, with only a dull dead thud from the boulder under it; then the stone hops twice and comes to rest, two quick lighter clacks, while chips and grit skitter off. Shortly after the hit a near wall of the gorge sends the crack back once, darker, with a ghost of a second return, and the rock around it gives a short dark wash.

tracks.note: The thrown stone: a small, flawed, irregular lump hit hard. Its bright click is the sound; two lighter hops follow as it settles.
The snap of the contact itself: a tiny burst of bright noise, grit crushed between the two faces.
The boulder: far too massive to answer with a note, so only a dull, dead, spread thud, a hair behind and well under the stone.
Chips and grit skipping away after the hit.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: Two pebbles clicking to a rock the size of a head landing: lower, longer, more thud.

controls.label: Force
controls.hint: A tap to a hard throw that snaps and knocks chips off.

controls.label: Stone
controls.hint: Soft crumbly sandstone that thuds, to glassy flint that clicks and rings a moment.

controls.label: Gorge
controls.hint: Open ground with no echo, or rock walls that throw the crack back.

controls.label: Wall distance
controls.hint: A near wall to one far across the gorge: a later echo.

patch.name: Rubber ball bounces to rest
patch.description: A solid rubber bouncy ball dropped from waist height onto a wooden gym floor. Each gap is shorter than the last by the same fraction and each hit softer, until the bounces run together into a short buzz and stop. Every bounce is the same ball: a round, pitched "pock" with the hollow floor answering under it, in a big empty gym.

tracks.note: The ball: one rubber sphere bouncing, each gap a fixed fraction of the last.

controls.label: Height
controls.hint: Dropped from a hand-width, or thrown down from overhead: longer gaps, more bounces.

controls.label: Bounciness
controls.hint: A dead ball that stops in three hops, or a super ball that will not quit.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A marble-sized super ball to a basketball.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: Solid concrete, or a hollow wooden floor that booms with each bounce.

controls.label: Gym
controls.hint: A small room to an empty sports hall.

patch.name: Heavy sack thud
patch.description: A heavy sack of grain dropped off a shoulder onto the plank floor of a barn. A soft, wide whump with no click at all, the burlap spreading rather than hitting; the floor planks boom once underneath; just after, the grain inside slumps with a dry hiss as it settles; a wooden room around it.

tracks.note: The sack landing: dark noise that swells and closes down, darkening as it goes. A spread, not a hit.
The planks: a big wooden cavity kicked by something soft, the pitch of the thud.
The contents slumping after the landing: a dry hiss of small grains.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A pillow to a body: lower, longer, more floor.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: Packed earth that gives nothing back, or a hollow stage that booms.

controls.label: Filling
controls.hint: A solid lump, or loose grain that hisses as it settles.

controls.label: Slap
controls.hint: A soft slump, or a flat landing with a leathery slap.

controls.label: Barn
controls.hint: Dry and close, or in a big wooden room.

patch.name: Trash can kicked
patch.description: A dented galvanised trash can kicked hard in a back alley. The boot lands on the thin steel wall with a dull bong and no tick; the wall is creased, so the clang is sour and uneven and buckles downward in pitch at the start; as the clang fades, the loose lid chatters on the rim, slowing to a stop; brick walls throw back a short hard echo.

tracks.note: The can wall: thin dented sheet steel hit by a soft boot. The pitch sag is the sheet buckling.
The loose lid rattling on the rim: a rolling chatter that slows to a stop.
The empty drum: the low breath of the can body under the clang.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A paint tin to an oil drum.

controls.label: Kick
controls.hint: A nudge with a sneaker to a full swing with a steel toecap.

controls.label: Dents
controls.hint: A new can with a clean clang to battered junk.

controls.label: Lid
controls.hint: No lid, or a loose one that chatters on.

controls.label: Alley
controls.hint: Open yard to a narrow brick alley.

patch.name: Fireball
patch.description: A fireball lit in the caster's hand and thrown. First the ignition, a soft 'whoomp' as the air catches: the flame's noise opening quickly from dull to bright, with a pressure thump under it. Then the ball roars and flutters like a torch swung through the air, and it travels away from you, so the roar drops in pitch, dulls and fades. All the way it spits and crackles: bright embers popping off and a few fat, low spits of resin, thinning as it goes.

tracks.note: Ignition: the pressure thump. A big soft membrane, not a sine drop, so it sounds like air and not a kick drum.
The flame: pink noise whose filter wanders at random and whose level flutters (a fast random tremolo); together they make it burn instead of hiss. Doppler carries it away.
Sparks and pops: sharp, uneven, never regular. Without them it is wind.
The fat in the fire: a few low, loud pops and spits of resin, scattered along the flight. They are what a listener calls 'fire'.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A candle-sized firebolt to a cart-sized ball of flame.

controls.label: Crackle
controls.hint: Smooth clean flame to a spitting, popping blaze.

controls.label: Flutter
controls.hint: A steady jet to a wildly guttering torch.

controls.label: Throw
controls.hint: Held burning in the hand, or hurled away fast.

controls.label: Ignition
controls.hint: How hard it catches at the start.

patch.name: Portal opening
patch.description: A doorway to somewhere else is forced open in a cave. It opens like a mouth: a deep buzzing drone (two sines grinding against each other) is shaped by a giant throat that moves from a closed 'oo' to a wide 'ah', climbing and growing as it goes. The rim spins: a rotor-like chop that starts slow and accelerates as the portal stabilises. Wind from the other side whistles through the gap, rising. Then it arrives: the gate locks open with a heavy stone thud that the whole cave answers, the drone at its loudest and widest. It holds open for a moment and then sinks back into the cave's long echo.

tracks.note: The portal's voice: cross-modulated sines for a thick, unstable buzz, then a formant filter with a huge throat. The vowel opening is the door opening.
Air from the other side: noise whistling through a tube whose note climbs as the gap widens. Wander keeps it gusting.

The edge burning: glittering metal shimmer from crackles, sparse at first and thickening, ringing a metal resonator. High and wide, chopped by the same spin as the drone, so the chop is heard as a turning edge.
The arrival: the gate locking open. A slab of rock taking the load all at once (a big stone plate, its blow slightly spread), a crowded low knock with no note of its own, thrown into the cave.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A keyhole rift to a gate a dragon could walk through.

controls.label: Opening time
controls.hint: Ripped open in a moment, or slowly prised apart.

controls.label: Spin
controls.hint: A still doorway to a hard-chopping vortex.

controls.label: Menace
controls.hint: A calm humming gate to a grinding, tearing wound in the air.

controls.label: Wind
controls.hint: How much air howls through from the other side.

patch.name: Sparkle pickup
patch.description: The hero's hand closes on a floating star shard. Five tiny glass notes run quickly up a pentatonic scale, each one a small bowl-shaped chime with its partials beating, the top one left to ring longer than the rest. As they rise, a puff of fairy dust goes up with them: separate pure pings, high above the notes, that climb and thin out and are still glittering after the last note. All of it in a bright plate so it glows instead of clicking.

tracks.note: The melody: the inharmonic partials of a glass bowl, not a synth beep. Slightly uneven timing and rising velocities so a hand could have played it.
The last and highest note: the same glass, left to ring longer than the run so the run arrives somewhere.
Fairy dust: separate pings, their range rising. This is what makes it magic and not a coin.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big warm gem to a tiny glittering shard.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: Short muted ticks to long singing glass.

controls.label: Dust
controls.hint: Just the notes, or a whole cloud of glitter around them.

controls.label: Glow
controls.hint: Dry and close, or hanging in the air.

patch.name: Spell cast
patch.description: A mage throws an arcane bolt. First energy is drawn into the staff: an unstable tone that wanders and climbs (an attractor being wound tighter), ringing a chord of sympathetic strings as it goes. Just before the release it holds its breath for an instant. Then the release. The staff head clangs, short, with strange overtones, and the bolt leaves: a tear of air, starting just ahead of the clang and as loud as it, that sweeps up, drops in pitch and dulls as it flies away from you. Behind it a trail of rising sparks, and the string chord left hanging in a stone hall.

tracks.note: Drawing power: a Lorenz attractor, speeding up and growing less stable as it winds. The string resonator turns its buzz into a chord, so the wind-up is musical. It cuts out for a moment before the release, so the cast hits out of a gap.

The cast itself: a short FM clang with inharmonic ratios whose brightness dies faster than its level, gone quickly so the tail belongs to the bolt, the sparks and the strings. Pitch kicks upward at the start, like something leaving.

The bolt leaving: air torn open, as loud as the clang at first, then carried away from you by the doppler (falling, dulling, fading). Starts just before the clang so the release has a leading edge. Without it the spell is only struck, never thrown.
What is left in the air: sparks that chirp upward, scattered along the bolt's path.

controls.label: Charge time
controls.hint: An instant snap cast to a long, wound-up incantation.

controls.label: Power
controls.hint: A cantrip, small and high, to a heavy, clanging great spell.

controls.label: Wildness
controls.hint: Disciplined, tonal magic to raw crackling chaos.

controls.label: Whoosh
controls.hint: How much air the bolt tears on its way out.

controls.label: Hall
controls.hint: Outdoors and dry, or echoing in a stone chamber.

patch.name: Chain rattle
patch.description: A length of steel chain hauled off a hook and dropped in a heap on a concrete floor. First the chain is dragged, links clinking against each other in a busy uneven patter, a few big links clanking low; then the run thickens into a rush as it slides off; then the pile lands and the last links trickle down and settle with a few separate clinks. A bare concrete room.

tracks.note: The links hitting each other: many small steel rings, busy then a rush then a trickle.
The weight of it: slack loops and big links clanking low, fewer and louder.
The heap landing on concrete: a gritty low scrape under the rush.

controls.label: Gauge
controls.hint: A fine necklace chain that tinkles to ship's anchor chain that clanks.

controls.label: Busy
controls.hint: A lazy sway with single clinks, to a frantic shake.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A short jerk on the chain, or a long haul.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: Held in the air, or dragged and dumped on concrete.

controls.label: Cell
controls.hint: Dry, or a bare stone cell.

patch.name: Clock ticking (loop)
patch.description: A wooden mantel clock on a shelf in a quiet room, looping one tick and one tock. Each beat is the escape wheel tooth dropping on a pallet, a tiny bright steel click, with a second fainter click just after as the pallet locks, and the clock's wooden case turning it into a soft hollow knock. The tock is a shade lower and duller than the tick, and the pair is not quite even, as in a clock slightly out of beat.

tracks.note: The escapement: steel tooth on steel pallet, drop then lock. Tick, then tock a shade lower.
The wooden case: the hollow knock that makes it a clock and not a relay.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A wristwatch held to the ear, to a grandfather clock in a hallway.

controls.label: Case
controls.hint: A bare movement, all click, or a resonant wooden case that knocks.

controls.label: Tick and tock
controls.hint: Two identical ticks, or a tick and a clearly lower tock.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: At your ear, or across a silent room.

patch.name: Motor starting
patch.description: A big workshop extraction fan motor switched on at the wall. The contactor slams in with a heavy clunk that rings its steel cabinet; the motor lurches from standstill, growling under load, and climbs to its running speed, the growl smoothing into a hum with a gear whine riding above it; it runs steadily for a moment, then fades as if you walked away.

tracks.note: The switchgear closing: a heavy relay clunk in a steel box.
The motor: from standstill to speed, load easing as it gets there.
The fan it drives: air building with the speed.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A desk fan to a ship's generator.

controls.label: Spin-up
controls.hint: Snaps up to speed, or takes its time getting a heavy flywheel moving.

controls.label: Age
controls.hint: New and smooth, or worn bearings that growl and wobble.

controls.label: Whine
controls.hint: A plain hum, or a gearbox that sings.

controls.label: Air
controls.hint: A bare motor, or one driving a big fan.

controls.label: Switch
controls.hint: A silent electronic start, or a contactor that slams.

patch.name: Ratchet
patch.description: A socket wrench swung back on its ratchet in a garage, held close: a quick run of teeth, starting fast and slowing as the wrist runs out of swing. Each tooth is three things in quick succession: the spring-loaded pawl drops off the tooth with a dry, bright steel tick (no note in it, a crowd of tiny partials gone at once), the forged head answers a hair later with a short dull knock, and then the pawl rides up the next tooth with a faint greasy scratch. The hollow handle hums very slightly behind the clicks. Uneven the way a hand is; a little garage behind it.

tracks.note: The pawl snapping into each tooth: a very short burst of bright noise through a tiny steel mechanism with a clustered chord of resonances, so every click is a dry dense tick, not a ping, with a faint ring of the hollow handle behind it. Pitch and level wander from tooth to tooth.
The forged head and gear taking each blow: a small irregular lump of steel, heavily damped by the hand and the grease, landing just after the tick. The dull knock that makes it a tool and not a toy.
The pawl riding up the next tooth against its spring: a few tiny greasy scratches between one click and the next. Quiet, but it is what makes the clicks a mechanism instead of a row of taps.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow deliberate click, click, click to a fast zip.

controls.label: Clicks
controls.hint: A short flick of a few teeth to a long swing.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A watchmaker's ratchet to a winch on a boat: lower, heavier, longer knocks.

controls.label: Slow down
controls.hint: Even clicks like a machine, or a swing that runs out of travel.

controls.label: Handle
controls.hint: A solid, dead tool, or a hollow chrome handle that sings a little with each click.

controls.label: Grease
controls.hint: A dry, scratchy, chattering ratchet to a freshly packed one with duller, softer clicks.

patch.name: Servo move
patch.description: A hobby-size robot arm servo turning its joint and stopping, heard close. The gear train takes up its slack with a small tick; the motor whines quickly up to speed, buzzes steadily, then strains and drops in pitch as it brakes against the load near the end of travel; it stops dead with a plastic clack of the gears settling. Its small plastic case makes it nasal.

tracks.note: The geared motor: spins up, holds, strains as it brakes.
The gears landing at the end of travel: a small hard plastic clack.
Backlash taken up at the start: a tiny tick.

controls.label: Travel
controls.hint: A small twitch to a long sweep of the arm.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow precise crawl to a fast snap: higher whine.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A micro servo in a toy to an industrial arm joint.

controls.label: Strain
controls.hint: Moving nothing, or fighting a heavy load: rougher, buzzier.

controls.label: Stop
controls.hint: A soft controlled stop, or slamming into the end stop.

patch.name: Spring boing
patch.description: A doorstop spring flicked with a toe: the cartoon boing. The coil is bent and let go with a metallic twang; it whips back and forth so the pitch wobbles widely, the wobble slowing and dying away while the whole note sags a little; the coil's overtones run away sharp of the pitch and chirp, the way spring reverbs do; a short dull wooden thunk from the skirting board it is screwed to.

tracks.note: The spring: a very stiff string, so its overtones go sharp and chirp. The LFO is the coil whipping about.
The wall it is screwed to: a short dull thunk at the flick.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A ballpoint pen spring to a car suspension coil.

controls.label: Wobble
controls.hint: A plain twang, or a wild whipping boing-oing-oing.

controls.label: Wobble speed
controls.hint: A slow drunken sway to a fast shiver.

controls.label: Coil
controls.hint: A tight wire that just twangs, to a loose slinky that chirps and splashes.

controls.label: Flick
controls.hint: A soft thumb to a hard fingernail: brighter twang.

patch.name: Toggle switch
patch.description: A chunky metal bat-handle toggle switch on an aluminium control panel, flipped up with a thumb, heard from the pilot's seat. First the lever passes centre with a small dull plastic tick. Then the spring throws the contact home, a hard, dry, dense clack (a crowd of tiny steel resonances gone at once, with the contact bouncing once just after), not a ping. At the same moment the thin panel it is bolted to takes the blow and answers with a short, boxy, slightly tinny "tok" that makes it sound mounted in something. Dry and close, like an aircraft cockpit.

tracks.note: The lever going over centre: the small dull pre-click, an irregular bit of plastic, heavily damped.
The spring-loaded contact landing and bouncing once: a tiny irregular steel part, many crowded modes, damped hard by its housing, so it is a dry clack. The Metal control lets it ring.
The panel the switch is bolted to: a thin damped sheet with many crowded modes (its lowest filtered off), hit through the switch body. The boxy tok that gives it a size.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A tiny slide switch to a big knife-switch breaker.

controls.label: Throw
controls.hint: A crisp short-travel click, or a long lazy lever with a gap between tick and snap.

controls.label: Panel
controls.hint: A bare switch in the hand, or one mounted in a hollow console that knocks.

controls.label: Metal
controls.hint: A soft plastic rocker, through a dry steel clack, to an all-metal toggle that rings.

patch.name: Cloth swish
patch.description: A cotton jacket sleeve as an arm swings out and back: two brushes of fabric on fabric, the answer a moment after the first, softer and lower. Each is a mass of fibres catching, so it is grainy rather than a hiss, swelling and thinning away with the speed of the arm; under the fibres the coarser threads of the weave drag over each other, a dry, pitchless, lower rasp that gives the cloth its body. Very close, dry.

tracks.note: The fabric: a dense cloud of tiny noise grains whose rate swells and dies with each move. Grain size is the coarseness of the cloth.

The threads of the weave dragging past each other: a fast scrape over a dead, lumpy, heavily damped surface (many crowded modes that die almost at once, so nothing rings and there is no note), a little lower on the way back. The dry rasp that makes it a jacket rather than paper or a hiss.

controls.label: Fabric
controls.hint: Silk, through cotton, to stiff canvas or leather: coarser, lower, louder weave.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow drag to a quick flick.

controls.label: Return
controls.hint: One move only, to a full back-and-forth.

controls.label: Layers
controls.hint: A single thin sleeve to a heavy coat or cape: denser rustle.

patch.name: Jump take-off
patch.description: A light runner in trainers and a tracksuit jumping straight up from the sprung wooden floor of a small gym (the same person and floor as "Soft landing"). First the legs drive and the boards take the load through the heels, a dull, dense knock with no note in it. As the weight rolls to the toes there is a second, lighter knock, and the rubber soles scrub and twist on the lacquer, a dry scuff with a short rising sneaker chirp in it as they let go. At the same time the body goes up through its own clothes, a grainy rustle of nylon that thins out as the feet leave, over a faint rush of air. No cartoon boing and no whoosh: the effort is in the push and the shoes.

tracks.note: The boards taking the push: a big damped wooden panel (many crowded modes, its lowest ones filtered off) loaded by a slightly spread blow, heel then toe. A dense low knock, not a drum.
